title: ‘Learning to export’ and ‘learning by exporting’: revisiting the relationship between innovation and exports in African firms
summary: The paper revisits the relationship between innovation and exports in African firms and finds a positive link running both ways. Innovation affects both whether a firm exports and how much it exports, and exporting makes innovation more likely.
keyFindings: Innovation raises both the likelihood and the intensity of exporting.
Exporting raises the likelihood of innovating; effects are mostly driven by direct exports and hold for product and process innovation.
Foreign ownership and international quality certification strengthen these effects.
methods: Cross-sectional World Bank Enterprise Survey data for 28 African economies, estimated with a censored Tobit IV simultaneous model with selection.
